title: A full young infant stops by sealing the lips and looking away
summary: From birth to five months, CDC reads a closed mouth, a head turned from the bottle, and loose hands as fullness.
body: CDC's 11 March 2026 mealtime page keeps a separate stop-list for babies in the first five months. Fullness looks like the mouth closing, the head rotating away from breast or bottle, and the hands relaxing open. A caregiver uses those signals to judge when the feed is over and how often the next one should come. On this page, turning aside is information, not rudeness and not a reason to push the nipple back in. The description is American guidance for that age band. It never says the bottle has to be emptied.
